cells.tense: You are here, with the pen, choosing one direction by what you actually feel.
cells.act: defend the direction you chose against the next push
cells.ask: You settled on a heading by feel, and something's still contesting it. The next time the pull comes to drift off it, decline once — one shove refused — and then say nothing about it.
cells.core:
You're steering by what you actually feel, and that's not softness — it's how you find the course. When two things want to move together, you allow that pull to be part of the deciding, and the thing you're heading toward gets closer instead of getting louder. People near this can tell the aim is honest, because you didn't argue it into place. You felt your way to it and stayed.

The pushback is coming — someone's doubt, a bad week, the old lean toward a safer heading. That's the test the direction wanted. Hold it once, against one real shove, and then leave the matter alone. Nobody needs you to guard it loudly all month; you're asked to stay the once it counts. The next step keeps the first one honest, and this steadiness is worth keeping precisely because you keep choosing it.
cells.sheetLine: Standing on what you feel is how the course gets made.
cells.verb: Choosing one direction through feeling and letting two ways of moving become one
cells.place: Standing where the pull toward what you want most is still clear

cells.tense: You are bracing for a version of this that hasn't been written yet.
cells.act: take pleasure in the grown thing
cells.ask: This week, enjoy something you already tended, on purpose — no next step, no fixing. Just the proof that it grew.
cells.core:
Somewhere in a connection that's genuinely going well, the aim has started running past the fact. You're picturing the next version, and then the one after, and the good thing that's here hasn't been looked at straight in a while. Force is moving in where feeling used to be. It doesn't look like pushing — it looks like care. But the other end of it can feel the grip.

What tends well is tending that doesn't exhaust. Rest in something already grown between you — no plan attached to it, no talk about where it's heading. Take pleasure in what arrived. If the picture gets quietly crowded while you do, that's fine; notice it and stay on the real thing. Care that holds without clutching stays. Watch it hold.
cells.sheetLine: You're already planning the next version of something that's going fine.
cells.verb: Choosing one direction through feeling and letting two ways of moving become one
cells.place: Standing where the pull toward what you want most is still clear

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you a long time ago.
cells.act: list the pulls on you and mark which are yours
cells.ask: Take what's pulling you toward what's next — people, directions, wants — and put it on paper. Mark the ones that are genuinely yours, and act on none of them this week.
cells.core:
Here, the aim has gone quiet. What you want is not arriving as a direction anymore — there's a lot of knowing about what other people are pointed toward, and very little about what draws you. Feeling has gone thin where you used to do the aiming. That's why the door remains open in your mind long after it's closed.

Seeing clearly is the way back — not pushing yourself to feel more. Lay out what's pulling you and separate it. Several will be true at once, and that's the point: many pulls, one that's yours. No acting, no strain, just the mark standing there. Perceptions come back when they're allowed to land without argument, and the direction is inside what you haven't claimed yet.
cells.sheetLine: The direction is there. It hasn't been separated from the rest.
cells.verb: Choosing one direction through feeling and letting two ways of moving become one
cells.place: Standing where the pull toward what you want most is still clear

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room you are already writing in and haven't noticed.
cells.act: show someone the way you found
cells.ask: Next time someone's weighing a direction, tell them plainly the way you found yours — a couple of lines, once — then let them walk it without managing what they do.
cells.core:
You are already steering other people through rough choices — showing them the passage, saying it once, letting them walk it. When asked, you say it's just how the thing works, no credit claimed. And the steering is real, and accurate. What's missing is the name on it.

The same instinct, turned back: what you can see for someone else is what you found for yourself first. When you give directions, stay in your own voice while you do it. Say the route the way you actually found it, not as if it came out of the air. Then let the person walk, and call the route yours. The way you see things is the way you came to see them, and that's not something to keep unclaimed.
cells.sheetLine: The route they're walking is one you found first.

attempts.check: The record calls the connection chosen and real, but two people entering one flow are not something either of them can verify from inside, so any claim that the other person is fully in it is mine to hold lightly. The reader's reasonable objection: 'You're calling something mutual that I'm still deciding, and my wanting might be the only clear thing in the room.' If I'm wrong, the asks still hold — they are acts of choosing, tending, noticing and naming, which stand whether the connection is solid or not. The sentence that serves me more than them: any line about two streams becoming one flow, which is the record's picture and not something I can say about a life I haven't seen.
